peer_review.summary:
The submitted work proposes an "Adaptive Resolution Substrate" as a meta‑reality that underlies our simulated universe, introducing novel constructs such as the simulation boundary resonance parameter (SBRP) and a latent scheduler variable. While the overarching question is intriguing and, if substantiated, would be transformative, the current manuscript falls short in several critical areas. The theoretical framework is presented qualitatively without a rigorous mathematical model, and the listed predictions are incomplete and lack quantitative detail. Moreover, the experimental proposals (e.g., controlled perturbation of the simulation boundary) are described only in vague terms, making them impossible to evaluate or replicate.

To move forward, the authors need to substantially flesh out the ARS model, provide explicit equations linking the proposed mechanisms to observable phenomena, and outline a concrete, testable experimental design. A thorough discussion of limitations, alternative hypotheses, and statistical power of the suggested measurements would also strengthen the work. Until these issues are addressed, the paper cannot be accepted in its present form.
